title: Efficient Coreset Selection with Cluster-based Methods

problem.claim: Coreset selection seeks to reduce training data while maintaining performance comparable to training on the full dataset.

gap.claim: Existing coreset-selection approaches can be time consuming, particularly gradient approximation on large training datasets because it requires multiple iterations and pairwise distance computations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Coreset selection selects a training-data subset intended to preserve full-dataset model performance.
Coreset selection may be performed with or without training models; training-free selection can occur before model training.
Training-based selection is time consuming, while gradient approximation can also be slow on large datasets due to repeated iterations and pairwise distance computations.
Gradient approximation is identified as the state-of-the-art approach for effectiveness.

unknowns: The proposed cluster-based method is not described.
No algorithmic details or theoretical guarantees are supplied.
No datasets, metrics, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions are supplied.
The relationship between computational efficiency and effectiveness is not reported.
